newsitem.title: NIGERIA: Slow Nigerian bourse expects increase in activity.
newsitem.headline: Slow Nigerian bourse expects increase in activity.

text.p: Shares rose slightly in dull Friday trading on the Nigerian stock exchange, but dealers said low bank interest rates were likely to lead more investors towards equities in coming weeks.
The all-share index closed at 7268.28 from 7263.28 on Thursday.
"With bank interest rates sliding, more investors will shift focus to shares to benefit from handsome capital appreciation," one dealer said.
Bank deposit rates are now in single figures, having fallen from 15/16 percent before the announcement of the 1997 budget almost two weeks ago.
Traders said that petroleum sector shares which slowed their advance because of fuel scarcity this week are likely to return to more promising performance from Monday.
Oil marketers Total and Texaco each rose five kobo on Friday to 63.85 naira and 38.45 naira respectively.
First Bank rose 10 kobo rise to 9.20 naira, while UBA, another of the big three banks, closed five kobo stronger at 7.50 naira.
Cadbury and Nestle each gained 10 kobo to end at 24.10 naira and 55.10 naira respectively.
Conglomerate UAC rose 10 kobo to 8.75 naira on an improved perception following recent acquisitions and expansions.
Healthcare company May and Baker advanced five kobo to 4.05 naira and insurance company AIICO six kobo to 12.76 naira.
Ashaka Cement was the biggest faller, down nine kobo to 14.10 naira, with large quantities of the stock on the market.
